sentences.text: The holotype specimen of Uragasaurus consists of a single anterior dorsal vertebra.
The vertebra was flattened from front to back as a result of taphonomic compression.
It is set apart from other mamenchisaurids by a teardrop-shaped pneumatic fossa at the tip of the transverse processes on that vertebra.
Uragasaurus is the first named member of the family Mamenchisauridae discovered in Thailand.
Fossils of Uragasaurus were recovered from the lower Phu Kradung Formation in Kalasin Province, northeastern Thailand.
The holotype specimen is curated at Mahasarakham University under the accession number PRC 460.
The genus and species were formally described in 2026 by Apirut Nilpanapan and colleagues.
Additional dinosaur bones were found near the holotype but cannot be confidently assigned to Uragasaurus.
Although only a vertebra is known, its close relatives possessed extremely elongated necks, suggesting a similar feeding strategy.
Uragasaurus is classified as a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur.
Phylogenetic analysis places it as an early-diverging member of Mamenchisauridae, after Tienshanosaurus and before Qijianglong.
It belongs to the class Saurischia, the “lizard-hipped” dinosaurs.
Uragasaurus lived between 149.2 and 137.05 million years ago, spanning the Tithonian to Berriasian stages.
Some researchers question whether the additional fossil fragments found near the holotype belong to Uragasaurus because they lack diagnostic features.
The phylogenetic relationships of Uragasaurus are considered weakly supported due to the fragmentary nature of the material.
